clue.text: Maiden is suitable to pinch

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
suitable means appropriate

explanation.surface: A girl deemed fit to steal something, perhaps a nervous accomplice being recruited.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch is slang for to steal, and to misappropriate is to take dishonestly what belongs to another.

clue.text: Show of force — organized army to toil at it

indicators.note: organized means arranged in order, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A display of strength, with soldiers set to labour at the task.
explanation.definitionFit: A military tattoo is a spectacular display of marching and music by armed forces, such as at Edinburgh.

clue.text: Mixed drink and crooned tune when upset

parts.note: crooned means sang

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A cocktail and a sung tune, as at a party turning sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine blended with fruit and lemonade.

clue.text: They take the lead, initially, with due respect to people like me

parts.note: pace is a Latin-derived preposition meaning with due respect to
the compiler is a setter, so people like the compiler are setters

explanation.surface: A setter politely acknowledging leaders, with deference to fellow compilers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacesetters lead a race in its early stages, setting the speed for the others to follow.

clue.text: Deserving member of crew

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as in meriting, to rate being to deserve
second meaning: a naval ... is an ordinary sailor

explanation.walkthrough: To rate is to deserve, so rating can mean deserving; it is also a non-commissioned seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating is a Royal Navy sailor without a commission, and rating something also means deserving it.

clue.text: Pathetic theatrical part I fit

parts.note: the pit is part of a theatre, the orchestra pit or old stalls
fit means able or capable

explanation.surface: An actor dismayed that the role they suit is a sad one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitiable describes something deserving pity, which is the sense of pathetic.

clue.text: Local European river

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a local is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub
second meaning: the ... flows through Switzerland, Austria and Germany

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'local' is the pub nearest home.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub or tavern, and the Inn is an Alpine river joining the Danube at Passau.

clue.text: Person nearly falling for a tourist

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who trips, stumbling
second meaning: a day tourist on an outing

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is someone who stumbles; the other is British for a day visitor on an excursion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is a holidaymaker on a short excursion, and literally one who stumbles.

clue.text: Batting quietly under strain perhaps, in stubborn fashion

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the last piece below the others

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word strain is one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: gently means quietly or softly

explanation.surface: A cricketer at the crease, playing calmly under pressure, but refusing to budge.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigent means refusing to compromise, so intransigently means in an obstinate, unyielding way.

clue.text: Fifty I count out for print, kind of

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters of count are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tallying fifty items before sending them off to be printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A linocut is a relief print made from a design carved into a block of linoleum.

clue.text: Strain is back in part of joint

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the joint part

parts.note: a tenon is the projecting piece of a mortise-and-tenon joint in carpentry

indicators.note: back says the word is should be read in the reverse direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A carpenter noticing stress where a joint's piece has been forced back.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is a state of stretching or stress, so it is a synonym for strain.

clue.text: One abandoning ship turned to sailor

indicators.note: turned means the word is flipped round to read the other way

parts.note: rats are proverbially the first to desert a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A deserter who defects to join a seaman, a story of shipboard betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar, short for tarpaulin, is old slang for a seaman, as in Jack Tar.

clue.text: Pray send up a novel as original source for this

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A plea to lampoon a work of fiction, as the satirical starting point for this very piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' is the crossword itself, which originally appeared in a weekend newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossword was first printed in the Sunday Telegraph, a weekly newspaper published on the Sabbath.

clue.text: David, for example, paints no art badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are poorly assembled and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist named David who paints with no skill at all.
explanation.walkthrough: David looks like a painter such as Jacques-Louis David; he is Saint David of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint David is the protecting holy figure of Wales, an example of a national guardian saint.

clue.text: Part of Venice included in ministerial tour

indicators.note: included in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A government minister's tour taking in a district of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the famous bridge and commercial district on the Grand Canal in Venice.

clue.text: Note club that was useful for press

parts.note: a flat is a musical note lowered a semitone
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A memo about a club that once had a use for the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatiron was an old heavy iron, heated on a stove, used for pressing clothes.

clue.text: Old magistrate imprisoning Prince I let off

indicators.note: imprisoning means the outer word holds the others captive inside it

parts.note: a reeve was a medieval local magistrate or official

explanation.surface: An old judge who has a royal in custody and then lets him go.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprieve is to cancel or postpone a punishment, sparing the condemned.

clue.text: Restricted movement for alien in debt

indicators.note: movement says the letters, alien included, shift about into a new order
for indicates that the alien stands in place of the IN of the debt phrase

parts.note: to be in debt is to be in the red
ET is the film's extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A borrower whose freedom of movement is curtailed because of what they owe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts ET in place of the IN of IN THE RED, giving ETTHERED; 'movement' then swaps the first two letters, so the alien's letters move.
explanation.definitionFit: A tethered animal is tied by a rope, so its movement is limited or restricted.

clue.text: Anarchistic author penning essays, primarily

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen holds animals
anarchistic means lawless and disordered, so the letters of author are jumbled
primarily takes the first letter of essays

explanation.surface: A writer of anarchist leanings who chiefly composed essays.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the man: Henry David Thoreau wrote the essay Civil Disobedience, admired by anarchists.
explanation.definitionFit: The American writer Henry David Thoreau, author of Walden, held anti-government views and was mainly an essayist.

clue.text: Person from one part of Africa thus leading another

definitions.text: Person from one part of Africa

indicators.note: leading puts the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: so means thus
Mali is another African country

explanation.surface: An African from one nation who is therefore in charge of a neighbouring one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Somali is a native or citizen of Somalia in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: High-rise accommodation for soldiers and others

definitions.text: High-rise accommodation for soldiers and others

parts.words: High-rise accommodation for soldiers and others
parts.note: soldiers are a caste of ant, and their mound home can be very tall

explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers' suggests army barracks, but soldier ants and workers live in a heaped insect nest.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect colony builds a mound of earth as its nest, sometimes several metres tall.

clue.text: Separate letter that may have French accent, acute or grave

parts.note: to sever is to separate

parts.words: letter that may have French accent
parts.note: in French the letter E can take an acute or grave accent

explanation.surface: A grammar note: split off a letter that bears an acute or grave accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acute or grave' seems to name the accents, but it is the definition: both words mean serious.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute illness or a grave situation is serious, and severe means serious or intense.

clue.text: After US resort, revised parts of voyage — they're not long in Bermuda

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the gathered letters are rearranged

parts.note: a leg is one stage of a voyage; the clue's plural is loose

explanation.surface: A traveller whose voyage stages were rearranged after a stop at an American holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog reads it as an anagram of US RESORT then LEGS, which leaves a spare S; an anagram of US RESORT plus LEG fits exactly. Bermuda shorts stop at the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: Bermuda shorts are knee-length, so in Bermuda the lower parts of a pair of pants are cut short.

clue.text: Beginning from two, ends in one or low digit

indicators.note: beginning from takes the opening letter of the word two
ends in takes the first and last letters of the word one

explanation.surface: Counting from two, ending in one, as if a countdown of small numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A toe is a digit of the foot, the lowest part of the body.

clue.text: Keep an eye on love poetry by European

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as O
verse means poetry

explanation.surface: Supervising romantic poems written by someone from the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise or watch over, which is what keeping an eye on something means.

clue.text: Slowly take liquid hydrogen out of vessel

indicators.note: out of means the element leaves the vessel word

parts.note: a ship is a vessel
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: Slowly drawing liquid hydrogen from a container, as in a laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid hydrogen' reads as a phrase, but 'liquid' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To sip is to drink in small mouthfuls, taking a drink a little at a time.

clue.text: Person who wants the best people in personnel, it is true

definitions.text: Person who wants the best people

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A staffing claim: among the employees, it is true, is a snob.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist believes society should be led by a select few, the elite or cream.

clue.text: Flexible in one's mind in relation to addition

parts.note: supple means flexible
mentally means in the mind

explanation.surface: Mental agility described as it applies to doing sums.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplement is an extra part, so supplementally means by way of an extra or additional part.
